title: Within Thy Courts My Praise Shall Rise
description: Within Thy Courts My Praise Shall Rise in Tonic Solfa to MELITA, doh is C: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 2 verses and a piano.
about: John Brownlie translated these words from the Greek service books for Hymns from the Greek Office Books (Paisley, 1904), headed “Stichera Idiomela”.
The book printed the words without tunes. They are in Long Metre, six lines (8.8.8.8.8.8), and this page sets them to MELITA; any other Long Metre, six lines tune fits them as well.
underlay: With-in Thy courts my praise shall rise, O Sa-viour of the world, to Thee; And while I bow, will lift mine eyes, Un-con-quered Might, Thy face to see; At eve, at morn, at noon, al-way, All bless-ing Lord, to Thee I'll pay.

lines: Within Thy courts my praise shall rise,
O Saviour of the world, to Thee;
And while I bow, will lift mine eyes,
Unconquered Might, Thy face to see;
At eve, at morn, at noon, alway,
All blessing Lord, to Thee I'll pay.
Here in Thy courts, O Lord, we bow,
And soul and body worship give;
Hear us, Thy faithful servants now,
Eternal God in Whom we live;
And Holy Spirit Three in One.

source: John Brownlie, Hymns from the Greek Office Books (1904)
licence: Public domain: John Brownlie died in 1925.
credits: Translated by John Brownlie (1857–1925) from the Greek, public domain, as printed in Hymns from the Greek Office Books; set to MELITA by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
